title: the WSG treading water
audit_label: R453 WSG treading water pin audit
audit_comment: The treading water slice pins the proficient calm-water hold (turns equal to twice the endurance score, one endurance point per two turns), the nonproficient limit (rounds equal to the strength score, modified for encumbrance the same way a swimmer's endurance is modified), the expiry checks (a Strength Check at expiration and every round thereafter, cumulative +1 after the first, per the 6-strength/12-round example), and the current rules (carried at the current speed modified for encumbrance, the proficient hold-position effectively swimming with endurance assessed, the nonproficient sinking immediately if he resists) (rules/wsgtread.h, prefix wtw); census 377 -> 378.

banner.title: The WSG TREADING WATER, R453: a character with swimming proficiency who is afloat in calm water can remain in one place, by treading water, for a number of turns equal to TWICE his endurance score - in other words, he uses up one endurance point for every two turns spent treading water. A character WITHOUT proficiency in swimming can safely tread water for a number of rounds equal to his STRENGTH score; this time limit is modified for encumbrance in the same way that a swimmer's endurance is modified. When the time limit expires, and at the expiration of every round thereafter, the character must make a Strength Check to remain afloat, and every check after the first one is made with a CUMULATIVE +1 modifier to the die roll. The printed example: a character with a strength of 6 who is not encumbered can tread water for at least 12 rounds - the strength limit doubled by the unencumbered endurance multiplier - with the unmodified check at the end of the 12th round, +1 at the end of the 13th, +2 at the end of the 14th, and so on. A character treading water in a current has no control over his movement: he is carried in the direction of the current at a rate equal to the speed of the current, modified for his encumbrance just as for swimming movement. A proficient swimmer can prevent himself from moving with the current and maintain the same position in the water - but then he is effectively SWIMMING, not treading water, and endurance is assessed accordingly. A nonproficient character cannot prevent himself from being carried along by the current; if he attempts to do so, he will begin to SINK immediately. Census 377 -> 378.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 43; the user own copy OCR (page 44) cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0043) - the section reads CLEAN two-way, every number (the twice-endurance turns, the one-point-per-two-turns rate, the strength-score limit, the cumulative +1 check modifier, the 6-strength/12-round example with the +1/+2 follow-on checks, and the sink-immediately rule) matched exactly; the only djvu garbles are the section header and word breaks - no eye-reads needed.
banner.sentinel: Tread calm water twice your endurance in turns, a point every two turns - or, without the skill, hold your head up for your strength in rounds, modified by encumbrance like endurance, then roll Strength every round at +1 a check while the current carries you off. Fight the current and swim, if you can - if you cannot, you sink.
